hash_lineage_note: raw = the untouched db pull output. previous_reviewed = after removing the pg_net teardown noise. reviewed = after the owner-authorized ACL replay normalization.
local_postgres_version: PostgreSQL 17.6 on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (GCC) 15.2.0, 64-bit
local_execution_method: print-sql from the unmodified tool, executed read-only with psql inside the local stack container. The tool was not modified. --source local is unusable on CLI 2.109.1: supabase db query --local rejects the multi-statement SQL with 'cannot insert multiple commands into a prepared statement'.

explained_platform_differences.difference: local has 6 extensions, hosted Staging has 5; the extra local extension is pg_net.
explained_platform_differences.explanation: The local Supabase stack installs pg_net by default; hosted Staging does not have it enabled. The generated capture emitted DROP EXTENSION pg_net as shadow-database portability noise, which was removed under the Section 16 bounded-noise protocol. Application impact: NONE.

normalization_log.reason: pg_net is platform-managed and lives in the extensions schema, not an app-owned public/private object. Keeping it would make the baseline tear down a platform extension on replay.

normalization_log.class: baseline portability / replay normalization (owner-authorized ACL normalization)
normalization_log.action: added 17 explicit REVOKE statements at the end of the baseline
normalization_log.objects: 14 application tables (FROM anon) and 3 functions (FROM PUBLIC, plus anon and authenticated on public.rls_auto_enable())
normalization_log.derivation: Every REVOKE was derived from the captured hosted Staging privilege facts (privileges.relations and privileges.functions detail lines). No privilege was guessed.
normalization_log.reason: A fresh replay inherits privileges from the stock ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statements in the capture and from PostgreSQL's default EXECUTE grant to PUBLIC. Hosted Staging objects do not hold those privileges, so the replay was more permissive than Staging.
normalization_log.staging_impact: NONE - these REVOKEs do not tighten Staging. They make a fresh local reconstruction match the privileges already present on Staging.

acl_normalization_detail.objects: public.action_records, public.discovery_answers, public.discovery_records, public.events, public.household_categories, public.household_members, public.household_systems, public.households, public.meal_plan_entries, public.needs_me_items, public.onboarding_state, public.one_move_records, public.profiles, public.tasks
acl_normalization_detail.hosted_privilege_state: no ACL entry at all; hosted relation grantees are exactly authenticated, postgres, service_role
acl_normalization_detail.incorrect_local_privilege_state: all 8 relation privileges (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER, MAINTAIN), inherited from ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES
acl_normalization_detail.revoke_added: REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.<table> FROM anon;  (one per table, 14 total)

acl_normalization_detail.hosted_privilege_state: EXECUTE held by authenticated and postgres only
acl_normalization_detail.incorrect_local_privilege_state: PUBLIC additionally held EXECUTE (PostgreSQL default for new functions)
acl_normalization_detail.revoke_added: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION private.is_household_member(text) FROM PUBLIC;

acl_normalization_detail.hosted_privilege_state: EXECUTE held by postgres and service_role only
acl_normalization_detail.incorrect_local_privilege_state: PUBLIC held EXECUTE by PostgreSQL default; anon and authenticated additionally held EXECUTE via ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ON ROUTINES
acl_normalization_detail.revoke_added: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.rls_auto_enable() FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated;

acl_normalization_detail.hosted_privilege_state: EXECUTE held by anon, authenticated, postgres, service_role
acl_normalization_detail.revoke_added: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.set_row_updated_at() FROM PUBLIC;
acl_normalization_detail.note: anon EXECUTE is legitimate on hosted Staging for this function and was deliberately PRESERVED. A blanket revoke would have broken parity.

deferred_finding_for_sd4.finding: The baseline retains the stock ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statements granting anon, authenticated and service_role on TABLES, SEQUENCES and ROUTINES in schema public. Any object created after this baseline will again inherit those grants unless the migration that creates it revokes them explicitly.
deferred_finding_for_sd4.status: recorded only, not changed in Phase 1
deferred_finding_for_sd4.rationale: Phase 1 reproduces current hosted privileges faithfully. Default-privilege policy for future objects is a schema-design decision.
